summary: One line that says which phase the agent is in: Thinking, Searching, Reading, Waiting for you, Writing and Done, each with its own glyph, over a track of six segments that fill phase by phase. When the agent needs a decision it stops the clock and asks, with Approve and Not now; when a phase runs long it says it is still working and offers Stop; when a step fails the line turns red and offers Retry. Once done it reads "Thought for 12s" and opens to the time each phase took.
use: Above an agent's reply, when people only need to know what stage it is at rather than every step.
When the agent can stop to ask for approval in the middle of its work.
Where the detailed trace (Thinking or Reasoning trail) would be too much, as a lighter companion to them.
features: Six phases, each with a glyph: turning dots, a radar, a page, a hand, a pen and a check. The phase's words shimmer while it lasts.
A track of six short segments: done phases fill in the accent, the phase in hand breathes, and the whole track turns green once done.
A timer that counts seconds by itself (or takes `seconds`) and pauses while it waits for you.
`ask`: in the waiting phase a tinted box asks the question, with Approve (primary) and Not now.
`slow`: a quiet line with a clock, "Still working…", and Stop when `onStop` is set.
`error`: the glyph and the line turn red, with the detail and Retry under it.
Done: the line reads "Thought for 12s" and becomes a button that opens the list of phases with the time each took (`took`).
a11y: A role="status" region announces each change of phase (and an error, and Done with the time), never every second.
Once done the line is a button with aria-expanded; before that it is marked aria-disabled.
Approve, Not now, Stop and Retry are real buttons, reached with Tab.
With reduced motion the turning dots, the radar and the breathing segment stand still.

faq.q: How is this different from Thinking?
faq.a: Thinking lists each step the agent takes and what it found. Agent phases says only which of six phases it is in, in one line, and handles the moments it needs you.
Yes. Move `phase` straight to the next one you need; the track fills up to it. Leave a phase out of `took` and it is left out of the finished list.

faq.q: When should I show the slow line?
faq.a: Whenever your agent decides a phase is taking long, for example after twice its usual time. Pass `slow` then, and clear it when the phase moves on.
